case.summary: The investigation found four online purchases on card C05851-K1, each just under a $500 authorization limit, made within 30 minutes on 2016-11-21. Evidence shows the same pattern on 11 other cards in a ±30-day window, indicating a coordinated scheme. The case was escalated to a fraud analyst, who confirmed the pattern and agreed it was fraud. The card was blocked, the transactions were declined, and a report was filed. The case remains open for monitoring of connected cards.

sar.narrative: Between 2016-11-21 10:00 and 2016-11-21 10:30, card C05851-K1 held by customer C05851 was used for 4 online transaction(s) totalling $1,911.84 (transaction IDs 3475403, 3475405, 3475408, 3475414). The activity came to the bank's attention through an analyst request on 2016-11-21 10:30:00, referring to transaction 3475414 for $488.00. The transactions were billed in region code(s) 420 (country code 87 unless noted), and the purchaser email domain was gmail.com. Online activity used the device profile C6743 Build/LMY47V | Android 5.1.1 | android browser 4.0 | 960x540. The activity fits none of the bank's five documented fraud patterns. Authorization-threshold structuring: 4 online purchases on one card, each between $400 and $500, inside about 30 minutes, from more than one device. The amounts look chosen to stay just under a $500 authorization limit. The same run shape appears on 11 other cards in the surrounding weeks, so it is a repeated scheme across customers rather than one compromised card. The same scheme links to other cards, which have been placed under monitoring: C00466-K1, C01890-K1, C02265-K1, C03633-K1, C05423-K1, C05766-K1, C06881-K1, C07297-K1, C10751-K1, C10990-K1, C12641-K2. Analyst confirms the repeated under-$500 run shape links 11 other cards with the same activity in the window and agrees it is one coordinated scheme. The card has been recommended for blocking and reissue, and the total suspicious amount reported is $1,911.84.
